annotations.title: Labor-hours test and the apprenticeship cure

description: The apprenticeship labor-hours requirement for one facility (26 CFR 1.45-8(b)): qualified apprentices must perform the applicable percentage (10% if construction began before 2023, 12.5% in 2023, 15% from 2024) of total labor hours, counting every contractor and subcontractor, after excluding hours of foremen, superintendents, owners and executive/administrative/professional staff, and counting apprentice hours only within the daily ratio. Returns the required hours, the shortfall, and the cure the IRS accepts: $50 per shortfall hour ($500 with intentional disregard), including participation failures (an employer with 4+ individuals and no apprentice: its labor hours divided by its number of laborers and mechanics).

construction_began.description: When construction began (YYYY-MM-DD or a year): sets the percentage.

counted_apprentice_hours.description: Hours worked by qualified (registered) apprentices that are within the daily ratio. Use check_daily_ratio to find them.

good_faith_hours.description: Apprentice hours covered by denied or unanswered good-faith requests (1.45-8(f)(1)); they count as apprentice hours.

intentional_disregard.description: true if the failure was knowing or willful (the IRS decides); the rate becomes $500 an hour.

participation_failures.description: Employers with four or more individuals on the facility and no qualified apprentice (each adds a participation shortfall).

individuals.description: Its number of laborers and mechanics on the facility over the construction.

labor_hours.description: That employer’s labor hours on the facility.

total_labor_hours.description: Total labor hours of construction, alteration or repair on the facility by all laborers and mechanics (every employer), apprentices included; hours of foremen, superintendents, owners and 541-exempt staff already left out.
